items: Hyperactivity of mesolimbic dopamine pathway at D2 receptors causes positive symptoms like delusions and hallucinations (StahlNeuro p.90).
Hypoactivity of mesocortical dopamine pathway to DLPFC and VMPFC causes negative and cognitive symptoms (StahlNeuro p.93-95).
PET imaging reveals increased dopamine synthesis and release specifically in the associative striatum (StahlNeuro p.92).
Blockade of D2 receptors in nigrostriatal pathway above 80% causes extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS) (StahlNeuro p.165).
Blockade of D2 in tuberoinfundibular pathway leads to hyperprolactinemia (StahlNeuro p.164).
key_numbers: 80% D2 occupancy threshold for EPS (StahlNeuro p.165)
5 classic dopamine pathways in the brain (StahlNeuro p.84)

items: Hypofunction of NMDA receptors on parvalbumin-positive GABAergic interneurons causes tonic disinhibition of cortical pyramidal neurons (StahlNeuro p.105-107).
Uninhibited pyramidal neurons produce a glutamate surge that overstimulates subcortical mesolimbic dopamine neurons, causing secondary hyperdopaminergia (StahlNeuro p.110).
Ketamine and PCP act as non-competitive NMDA open-channel blockers, inducing positive, negative, and cognitive symptoms of schizophrenia (StahlNeuro p.105, p.108).
NMDA receptor opening requires co-agonists D-serine or glycine alongside glutamate and depolarization to remove the magnesium plug (StahlNeuro p.100).
key_numbers: 3 conditions required for NMDA opening: glutamate, D-serine/glycine, and Mg2+ removal (StahlNeuro p.100)
2 co-agonists required at NMDA glycine site: D-serine or glycine (StahlNeuro p.99)

items: 5-HT2A receptor hyperfunction on apical dendrites of cortical layer V pyramidal neurons induces hallucinogen-like glutamate release (StahlNeuro p.125, p.131-132).
Atypical antipsychotics (SGAs) are defined by 5-HT2A receptor antagonism/inverse agonism equal to or exceeding D2 affinity (StahlNeuro p.183-188).
5-HT2A antagonism in the substantia nigra disinhibits dopamine release, reducing EPS risk in the motor striatum (StahlNeuro p.185).
5-HT2A antagonism in the VTA disinhibits dopamine release to the prefrontal cortex, improving negative symptoms (StahlNeuro p.186).
key_numbers: 5-HT2A >= D2 binding affinity ratio defines atypical antipsychotics (StahlNeuro p.183)

items: Structural MRI/CT consistently shows lateral and third ventriculomegaly and medial temporal/hippocampal volume reduction (DSM p.114; Dulcan p.391).
fMRI demonstrates DLPFC hypofrontality during working memory and executive functioning tasks (Dulcan p.391; StahlNeuro p.449).
Childhood-Onset Schizophrenia (COS) shows progressive cortical gray matter loss moving parietally to prefrontally during adolescence (Dulcan p.391, p.405).
DTI reveals reduced fractional anisotropy in white matter tracts, supporting the neural dysconnectivity hypothesis (Dulcan p.91, p.391).
key_numbers: 2% to 5% reduction in total brain volume (Dulcan p.391)
3rd and lateral ventricles enlargement (DSM p.114; Dulcan p.391)

etiology.genetic: Heritability ~70%-80%; polygenic common variants (PRS) and rare structural CNVs like 22q11.2 deletion (Dulcan p.118, p.390; DSM p.114).
etiology.neurobiology: NMDA hypofunction on GABA interneurons leading to cortical disinhibition and mesolimbic hyperdopaminergia at D2 receptors (StahlNeuro p.90, p.105).
etiology.environmental: Adolescent high-potency cannabis use, obstetric hypoxia, maternal infections, urbanicity, and advanced paternal age > 60 (Dulcan p.391; StahlNeuro p.149).

high_yield: DSM-5-TR Criterion A requires at least 2 psychotic symptoms for 1 month (minimum 1 being delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized speech) with total duration >= 6 months (DSM p.114).
Childhood-Onset Schizophrenia (COS) onset < 13 years is associated with insidious onset, severe premorbid delays, and high CNV burden (Dulcan p.389, p.391).
22q11.2 deletion syndrome is the strongest single genetic risk factor, conferring a 25%-30% lifetime risk of schizophrenia (Dulcan p.118, p.391).
C4 allele variations in MHC locus 6p22 drive excessive microglia-mediated synaptic pruning during adolescent brain maturation (Synopsis ch.33 Neural Sciences).
5-HT2A antagonism disinhibits nigrostriatal and mesocortical dopamine release, mitigating EPS and improving negative symptoms (StahlNeuro p.185-187).
